verdict.tagline: Big open world ambition hindered by persistent launcher and performance hurdles.
for_you_if: you want a sprawling open world to explore
you can overlook repetitive side activities
you are willing to master heavy driving mechanics

you cannot tolerate startup crashes or login blocks
you need smooth and responsive PC controls

Ubisoft presenting cool concept with mixed execution!

The Story is a missed opportunity as it takes the generic revenge story and follows it heavily even thought Ctos and the underground gangs were so much more interesting than Aiden's own agenda. Even the idea of Aiden being a vigilante is just shoehorned in as its never really discussed until the end of the game which is only mention in small detail. The Characters were nothing special to talk about and while the conflict with Aiden and his morality was a neat idea, it was not conveyed all that well.

The Setting and Level Design are nothing to write home about as they pretty much follow the Ubisoft formula that we all either love or hate (I really don't like it). The only area that had any interest was Pawnee as it felt distinct from the other locations in the open world, however the rest of the open world just feels copied and pasted from others in the genre and by the studio.

Visually, its starting to show its age. Performance was interesting as while there was only one crash through my entire playthrough, the visual bugs such as lighting and the physics of NPC's and Aiden's coat really made the experience less immersive. While the game tries to go for a dark and grimey aesthetic, there really isn't that much of an art direction as many locations and designs are just bland and quite forgettable.

Sound and Audio are probably the most frustrating parts of the game as the entire experience sounded like it was on 5% volume and I tried fixing this but to no avail. From what I could barely hear, the soundtrack was decent and the audio design was typical. 

In terms of Gameplay, I like some of the ideas that are on display, however the whole experience was just mediocre. I think the hacking that the game offers was a really cool idea and aids in many senarios, but the other stuff such as combat, driving, enemies, missions, etc are all repetitive and don't really offer any variation to what other open worl…

I finished the game yesterday and my friend asked me how it was, here's what I wrote back...

I appreciate many things about it, really.

For the first of it's kind, both in the industry and from ubisoft themselves, it's impressive how refined the hacking aspect feels. It feels natural enough—even if I ended up changing the controls to match watch dogs 2—to feel less like an aspect and more proper part of the game; if that makes sense.

The map is very good and surprisingly diverse for what is only supposed to be chicago. You have pawnee which is a more countryside region with a little, personal town next to "the loop" which is straight up downtown. Each area of the map, especially downtown, feels crafted to be useable in just about every scenario. You can walk around and it feels build for it, or drive through slowly and you'll get a nice view, maybe choose that path during a chase and you have the option to hack something to loose your persuers; it just feels well thought out.

The story is absolutely amazing. It feels realistic enough to stay believable but isn't so bound to reality that you feel restricted by it. It's really personal and you feel less like a player playing a character and more like you're actually Aiden (the person you play as). He's so well thought out that the line between you as the player and him as a ficional character merge really well. I personally haven't dealt with a lot of what he goes through in the story but I understood him perfectly, which I think is just thanks to the fire writing.

The ending is great and it actually lets you choose who you want Aiden to be going forward. I'm not gonna spoiler but you clearly choose if you let Aiden finish this chapter of his life and continue as a seperate event or continue doing the same thing that you started as since it's fundamentally the same thing but clearly seperated by intent.

Other characters are also understandable and their behaviour feels "justified"/natural which is always hard to…

Watch Dogs actually aged pretty well. It has an interesting enough story with a flawed protagonist who you want to succeed despite his hypocritical ways. The stealth gameplay is fun. The world is well made and has an immersive atmosphere. You could drive around listening to the radio and have a good afternoon. There's some flaws, some buggy missions, some frustrating overlooked level designs, and going for 100% completion or just filling out the map is too much and too tedious. The DLC is more of the same and just as lame as the random side objectives. But, overall, the game has a good story and is a nice experience that I'm glad I played. I recommend Watch Dogs but not to completionists.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes side content and activities that feel very repetitive.

citations.review_text:
Overall a really great game. Imagine if GTA actually took its story and world seriously plus added fun hacking.

Pros:
- Hacking abilities
- Skill tree is optional but adds a lot.
- Every playstyle works.
- Stealth options are really good
- Reputation system adds some fun nuance
- Great plot twists.

Cons:
- Escaping the police can be a pain
- Cars don't aways handle well (but motorcycles handle amazing)
- Side content is very repetitive.
- *Ubisoft 3rd party software required.

If the game is so good why am I downvoting? On principle, I downvote any game that requires 3rd party software or launchers to work. Steam games should only require steam. Any Ubisoft programs that are not the game itself should be optional.

The original Watch Dogs is still the best game in the franchise when it comes to story and atmosphere. While it lacks some of the gameplay refinements introduced in the sequel, it delivers a much darker and more grounded experience that actually takes itself seriously 

Aiden Pearce is easily the strongest protagonist in the WD series. He's far from a perfect person, but his motivations are understandable, and his journey of revenge feels personal from start to finish. The supporting cast isn't particularly memorable, but they fit the tone of the game well, and the villain has a much stronger presence than in the later entries I would say (ehh)

Gameplay can feel a bit dated by today's standards. Driving is heavier, parkour is limited, and hacking isn't nearly as advanced or creative as it is in Watch Dogs 2. However, the core mechanics still hold up surprisingly well for older standards

Chicago is one of the game's biggest strengths. Its gloomy weather, rainy streets, and realistic atmosphere perfectly complement the darker narrative. Unlike the vibrant and colorful San Francisco in the sequel, Chicago feels dangerous and believable, making exploration immersive even if the world isn't as interactive

The game isn't without flaws obviously. Some missions become repetitive, the side content is very generic and SOOOOO repetitive (especially if you're a completionist or just an achievement hunter), the gunplay is fairly standard but you can't shoot out of cars..? Well okay. The biggest let down was the game not living up to E3 standards back when the game was revelead

One thing to point out is the game being sold without an ONLINE license on Steam. This forces you to either buy the Ubisoft version and then transfer it to steam OR contact ubisoft through customer support to ask for an activation key (lord knows the patience you must have to do this). Another ubislop special wohooo

Overall, Watch Dogs remains the strongest entry in the franchise for playe…

After years of having played this game back in the day on the Xbox 360, I finally decided to go back and 100% Watch Dogs, including the DLC.

I have to say, this game is just as awesome as I remember it being. It definitely still has some of the jank and rough edges people mentioned back in the day, but a lot of that has been fixed up over the years, and the game has aged surprisingly well.

The story is amazing, and the Bad Blood DLC story is great as well. My only real gripe after all these years is how repetitive some of the base game side missions can be. I was hoping they might have improved that with the DLC, but unfortunately, that repetition is still there.

Overall, though, I absolutely recommend this game. If you played it back in the day or never got around to trying it, Watch Dogs is definitely worth playing. An amazing game that still holds up all these years later.

Side note: I’m also super happy that I was able to find people to do the online achievements with. As someone who absolutely hates online achievements, I was happy to see that the community for the base game is still somewhat active. Good luck finding someone for the DLC achievements, though. Luckily, I found someone on the forums who was in the exact same boat as me, so we were able to knock them out together.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the open world map of Chicago is large, but the city environment feels bland and lacks vibrant life.

Just now completed the story and what an amazing game!!
Played this purely because i wanted to try it for years after seeing so many youtube vids of it. DID NOT DISAPPOINT!! Driving takes a while to click, but once it does, it feels amazing, especially on the sports bike, it feels like being Batman with the cape flowing and all,
Chicago is big and fun to drive around, though the city hotspots feel unnecessary and a bit annoying. Hacking mechanics were fresh, but the gadget wheel navigation is janky, often times i found myself circling through it trying to grab the right item while enemies close in. I wasn't gaming around the time of the infamous E3 downgrade controversy, so I don't carry the same hate some people have for this game. Story was decent, ending was good and overall a really solid game.

Just finished the main story. 

It’s a fun ride overall, even if the narrative leaves a bit to be desired and falls flat sometimes. The story is pretty serious but [spoiler] the ending is kinda sad. [/spoiler]

The map is massive, but the open world feels pretty bland. It works fine as a backdrop for missions, but Chicago lacks the vibrant life that makes you actually want to explore it.

That said, the hacking mechanics are great. 
Combining stealth with manipulating cameras and traffic lights is genuinely satisfying and saves the gameplay loop.

Also, the Ubisoft launcher is an absolute nightmare to deal with and constantly ruins the experience before you even launch the game. Online doesn't even work on the steam version by default: you have to fix it yourself by buying the game on Ubisoft connect and then refunding it.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the Steam version requires dealing with a third-party launcher, Ubisoft Connect.

citations.review_text:
Pretty Good Game... but there are a lot of issues like the fact that I had to use another email account because ubisoft connect does not like my current steam email, and the fact that I have to make an account in the first place. Ubisoft Connect is just not needed imo. 

Also, for an old game, there are loads of funny glitches which I encountered like citizens just become statues for some reason. There are also some missions that were just lacking, especially on the Iraq Fight, that was just bad. Also, I think there's a problem with the online features, they're not working.

The Good: Graphics are nice. I LOVE the Mechanics, especially the hacking. And the game really forces you to be sneaky as you die really easily. World building is nice like CTOS, hotspots, crime prevention, soundtrack and etc. The soundtrack is fitting to the game, especially that part in UNINVITED. The GUI is very suited for the game something we lost in modern day games. Although I wish I got a reward for filling the reputation bar either on the left or right side. 

Game is a bit underwhelming for some reason, but if you can get a DEAL with this game, it's an experience. Its like they planned a lot to implement in the game but it still feels small. The shops is the funniest part as I never used them throughout my playthrough and for some reason they only offer 1 thing. LOL.

TLDR: Game's Fun, Get it when on Sale!
